Contrary to this theory, it states in section III.2 that four land parcels will hold "medium-rise apartments with less than 100 dwellings units each." In addition there will be "20 other parcels which will be converted to single-family residential." This amounts to approximately 400 new dwelling units which is 25% of the existing number of dwelling units. Since the project will displace only 49 individual residents from 110 residences, the redevelopment housing constitutes a significant increase in population. Therefore, it should be determined whether this population increase will have an impact on the project area.
On page 85, section IX, it states that "at least 51% of all housing units constructed therein (the project area) be for low-moderate income families and individuals, and no less than 20% be for low income facilities and individuals." This would seem to clearly define the economic cross-section to be achieved in the redevelopment housing. However, section II.6.h, the Economy, indicates the economic cross-section of the City of Harrisburg in general and not the specific project area.
Therefore, we suggest that:
a. The existing economic cross-section of the project area be determined from the 1970 census package. This data may be obtained from the Tri-County Regional Planning Commission or the City of Harrisburg.
b. Since the population change is significant, the existing economic cross-section should be compared to the federally mandated economic cross-section of the redevelopment housing.
c. If a significant difference exists between the two economic levels, its impact on the socio-economic environment should be evaluated in section V.3.
I hope these comments are self-explanatory, but if any clarification is necessary, please contact Bruce Bigelow of this office (787-7883).
